clue.text: Saint George, shocked by such discrimination

indicators.note: shocked suggests the letters of the saint's name are jolted into disorder

explanation.surface: England's patron saint is appalled by a particular form of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' scrambles SAINT GEORGE; 'by such' links the anagram to its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Separating people by race or group is a form of unfair discrimination, synonym-level.

clue.text: Parson crazed with love for a trebly gifted female

indicators.note: crazed means driven wild, so the letters of parson are thrown into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A clergyman, mad with passion, chooses a woman with many talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trebly gifted' is the pun: she is gifted in the treble range, the highest singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice is the treble range, so a gifted high singer is this voice type.

clue.text: Space-man yawned

parts.note: a space or opening is a gap
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: An astronaut gave a big yawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space-man' reads as astronaut but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stood open-mouthed, wide open, is a synonym of having yawned.

clue.text: Wrong, or sure one is wrong

indicators.note: words that are wrong are in the wrong order, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are mistaken, or that a single item is in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' appears twice: first as the definition, then in 'is wrong' as the anagram signal for OR SURE ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken or incorrect, a straightforward synonym for wrong.

clue.text: Flags and sail will need adjusting

indicators.note: adjusting the word sail means rearranging its four letters

explanation.surface: Bunting and a boat's canvas have to be set right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like a noun, banners, but is a verb: weakens.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or grow feeble, as does someone who is unwell, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Popular individual is actually present

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
an individual is a person

explanation.surface: A well-liked figure has turned up in the flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Being physically there rather than represented by someone else is a common idiom.

clue.text: Recess in pleasant hospital

indicators.note: in places the hospital letter inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: pleasant means nice
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A break spent in an agreeable hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' tempts as a holiday break, but here it is an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove or hollow set into a wall is a recess, a synonym.

clue.text: Predict vocal quartet will go to Ely perhaps

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the number word for a quartet is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a quartet is four
Ely is a cathedral city and bishopric, so an example of a see

explanation.surface: A singing foursome is said to be heading to the Cambridgeshire cathedral city of Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocal quartet' looks like a singing group, but 'vocal' only says the word four is spoken. A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is one in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something coming in advance is to predict it, a synonym.

clue.text: Perfume the French sell with hesitation

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to vend is to sell
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A French shopkeeper hesitates while selling a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant's fragrant oil is a classic scent, so its name stands for a perfume.

clue.text: Device preventing leaves from spreading around

definitions.text: Device preventing leaves from spreading around

parts.words: Device preventing leaves from spreading around
parts.note: leaves suggests foliage blowing about, but they are sheets of paper held together by a small bent wire

explanation.surface: A gadget that stops autumn foliage scattering everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent-wire office fastener holds sheets of paper, or leaves, together.

clue.text: Yet it provides academic standing

parts.note: the joke is that a seat is for sitting, yet a professorship gives high status in a university

explanation.surface: Something paradoxically grants scholarly status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yet' points to the paradox: an item for sitting gives 'standing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called by the name of the seat of office; it gives rank in a university.

clue.text: Study painting externally, being passionate

indicators.note: externally means the painting word sits on the outside, wrapping the study

parts.note: painting is art
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: Someone examines a canvas from the outside, fervently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb but is the room, a den.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervent and eager, a direct synonym of passionate.

clue.text: Plants for sycophants

definitions.meaning: climbing or trailing plants such as ivy
people who fawn and toady to win favour

explanation.surface: Greenery chosen for flatterers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing vines are one sense; fawning bootlickers who crawl to superiors are the slang second sense.

clue.text: A speaker returning brief thanks amid golden words

indicators.note: amid places the reversed thanks in the middle of the golden words

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold, and two words means two of them

indicators.note: returning means the word for brief thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is a short, informal thank-you

explanation.surface: A public speaker giving a quick thank-you amid eloquent golden phrases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golden words' sounds like eloquence, but in heraldry the word for gold is 'or', and the plural asks for two of them, flanking the reversed thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker who makes formal addresses, a synonym.

clue.text: One who can't remember me, as I can recollect

indicators.note: read as re-collect: gather the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful insists they can recall this speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollect' seems to mean remember, ironic beside the definition, but is the anagram signal, read as re-collect, for ME AS I CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering memory loss, so one unable to recall things.

clue.text: Time for breakfast food

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
oat cereal cooked in milk or water

explanation.surface: It's the hour to eat the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang this is time spent in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot oatmeal is a breakfast dish; the same word is British slang for a jail term.

clue.text: Unexpectedly meet resistance — woman in angry mood

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Una is a woman's name
someone in an angry mood is cross

explanation.surface: Running into opposition from a furious woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon someone by chance is an idiom for an unplanned meeting.

clue.text: Declare in favour of petitioner's cause

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
the case a petitioner makes is a claim

explanation.surface: Announcing support for someone's petition.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce publicly or formally is a synonym of declare.

clue.text: Cars go for service

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Vehicles going in to be serviced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like car maintenance but means religious or government service. The Mini is a small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministry is the work of a clergyman, a form of religious service, and also government service.

clue.text: Urchin lad wandering in gloom

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled lad inside the word for gloom

parts.note: murk is darkness or gloom

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so lad is rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy roaming about in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' scrambles LAD to DLA, which goes 'in' MURK.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a child scavenging on river mud, the word came to mean a street urchin.

clue.text: Catch the blame after net is damaged

indicators.note: after puts the blame word following the scrambled net
a damaged net has its letters knocked out of order

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: A fisherman gets blamed once the net is torn.
explanation.definitionFit: To snare or trap someone is to catch them, a synonym.

clue.text: Make an introduction here and now

definitions.meaning: to introduce someone formally, a verb sense
existing at this moment, the adjective sense

explanation.surface: Introduce someone right away.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing a guest is the verb sense; current, at this time, is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Length that boxers will go to, to avoid KO?

definitions.meaning: a span or extent of space

definitions.text: that boxers will go to, to avoid KO
definitions.meaning: a boxer who lasts every round without being knocked out is said to go the full course

explanation.surface: How far fighters will travel to avoid a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Space between points is a length; boxers who survive every round are said to go it.

clue.text: Tears shed for Flora

indicators.note: shed suggests the letters are cast off and fall in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over a woman called Flora.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a name but means plant life.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden plant is an example of flora, the plant world.

clue.text: Time when all assets were frozen?

definitions.text: Time when all assets were frozen?

parts.words: Time when all assets were frozen?
parts.note: frozen assets is a financial phrase, but here it means everything literally covered by glaciers

explanation.surface: A financial crisis when every account was locked.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric period when glaciers covered much of the world, so everything was frozen.

clue.text: Knowing a monarch should be held in high regard?

indicators.note: held in puts the a and monarch letters inside the word for high regard

parts.note: awe is great reverence
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Wise people know that a sovereign deserves reverence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conscious of something is knowing it, a synonym.

clue.text: Take a look at part of Tuscany

indicators.note: part of means only some letters of the Italian region's name are used

explanation.surface: A tourist glances at a region of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance over or examine is a synonym of take a look at.

clue.text: Expect a hold-up

parts.note: a delay or hold-up is a wait

explanation.surface: Anticipate a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' suggests a robbery but means a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To look forward to or wait for something is to expect it.

clue.text: On a charge after disturbance in port

indicators.note: after being disturbed the letters of on a charge are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone arrested following a riot at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where ships drop anchor, so a harbour or port; also a city in Alaska.

clue.text: Evocative of not long ago with short skirts being in

indicators.note: being in puts the short skirts inside the word for not long ago

parts.note: recent means from not long ago
minis are miniskirts

explanation.surface: Miniskirts are fashionable again, calling a recent era to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' reads as being fashionable, the surface sense, but its job is to place the skirts inside the phrase for not long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings memories back is evocative of the past, a synonym.
